_comment: Shared OCR CJK join cases, read by internal/ocr (joinLineWords, joinPlateLines) and extension/src/ocr-text.js (joinLineWords, joinPlateLines). A word is [text, x0, y0, x1, y1] in recognizer pixels. Words that meet on Han, kana or CJK punctuation join with no space; a pair involving Hangul joins only when the gap between the boxes is under OCR_HANGUL_JOIN_GAP_RATIO (0.33) x the median word height; every other pair keeps its space. Plate lines join the same way on Han, kana and CJK punctuation; a Hangul line break keeps its space (OCR-PIPELINE amendment 1.8). See docs/PARITY.md, CJK word join.

words.about: ja-comic-peppercarrot-p03: the recognizer cut one Japanese line into single characters
zh-comic-peppercarrot-p03: a fullwidth comma joins like the Han around it; the ASCII exclamation mark keeps its space
ko-comic-peppercarrot-p03: syllables 2 px apart join, the real word space (16 px on a 30 px median) stays
Hangul just under the bound: a 9 px gap on a 30 px median is under 9.9 px
Hangul at the bound: a 10 px gap on a 30 px median is not under 9.9 px
Hangul beside Han (hanja) is judged on the gap, like Hangul beside Hangul
Hangul with no measurable word height keeps its space - there is nothing to measure the gap against
the prolonged sound mark is Common script but joins like the katakana around it
a space between a CJK character and a Latin word or a digit is kept
